name: SWERVE
source: Sandia Winged Energetic Re-entry Vehicle (SWERVE). Three flights 1979-1985 from the Kauai Test Facility on STRYPI boosters; flight 3 reentered near Johnston Island (~1,180 km). Spherically blunted 5.25-deg half-angle cone, 'a little over 100 in' long (~2.6 m), with small wings/elevons for lift and control, Mach 2-14 maneuvering. Nose-tip/heat-shield ablative. Flight-3 maneuver (Williamson, AIAA 92-3989, Fig. 20): ~-10 deg AoA push-over at 20 s/Mach 12, +10-15 deg pull-ups, ~4 deg control deflection; all flight data (Figs 20/23/24) end at ~160 s. (The AHW conical glide body is described as 'SWERVE with improved TPS'.)
notes: GEOMETRY sourced: 5.25-deg sphere-cone, nose_radius from published R_n/R_base=0.07 (R_base=L*tan(5.25)~0.238 m -> R_n~0.0167 m). base diameter 0.476 m is the CONE base; the ~0.61 m (2 ft) factsheet 'diameter' includes the wings. MASS 185 kg and L/D 0.6 are CALIBRATED against four flight observables of flight 3 on Strypi VIII R (Kauai launch): (1) ~160 s reentry->impact window (Figs 20/23/24), (2) peak reentry ~Mach 12 (Fig 20), (3) ~1,180 km Kauai->Johnston range, (4) apogee in the documented 400,000-600,000 ft band (model ~630 kft, ~6% high). This supersedes an earlier 350 kg / L/D 1.5 guess that was calibrated to GLIDE range only and gave a 406 s descent (2.5x too long) and only Mach 10: SWERVE did NOT sustain a long equilibrium glide -- it reentered fast (~160 s) with maneuvers. The 185 kg is also consistent with beta=15,250 and a realistic sharp-5.25-deg-cone Cd~0.068 (m=beta*Cd*A). L/D 0.6 reflects the 'small wings', NOT the AHW model's 1.5. guidance=damped_glide models the maneuvering pull-up/push-over phugoid (Thrusty has no prescribed-AoA-schedule mode, so the exact Fig-20 alpha program is documented here, not flown). tps_material=carbon_ablator is the ORIGINAL ablative heat shield; the SWERVE->AHW claim is airframe reuse with an improved shield for AHW's much longer (~3,770 km) range -- AHW differs mainly in TPS and booster (STARS), not airframe.
